findings.evidence: grep for `wickRotation` in ./code returns only the def and the three lemmas at Basic.lean:219-242; the def's docstring (Basic.lean:216-218) and Uniqueness.lean:52-57 both assert the real-points/Euclidean-section correspondence, which `wickRotation_ofReal` states only pointwise.
findings.fix: Add the section-level lemma, e.g. `wickRotation ⁻¹' (euclideanSection d) = minkowskiSection d` (or the image/`Submodule.map` form) plus `wickRotation_symm_apply_inl`/`_inr` as `@[simp]`.
findings.issue: `wickRotation` is exposed with forward component lemmas only (`wickRotation_apply_inl/_inr`, `wickRotation_ofReal`). The structural property both new module docstrings invoke to justify it — that it matches the real points (`minkowskiSection`, i.e. `mem_minkowskiSection_iff`) with `euclideanSection`, making the latter maximal totally real — is stated nowhere, and `wickRotation.symm` has no component API, so a consumer transporting a domain along the rotation (as `Uniqueness.lean:81-92` does) must unfold the definition.

findings.evidence: Uniqueness.lean:121-133: `let w := v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0)`, `hwE`, `hw0`, `hw` are all local `have`s consumed only by the final `exact`.
findings.fix: Extract it as a public lemma (next to `ofMinkowski_mem_euclideanSection_iff` in `Continuation/Basic.lean`, or above the theorem in this file), e.g. `causalCharacter (v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0)) = .spaceLike ∧ ofMinkowski (v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0)) ∈ euclideanSection d` for spacelike `v`, and use it here.
findings.issue: The fact that the equal-time projection `v - v.timeComponent • basis (Sum.inl 0)` of a spacelike `v` is again spacelike and lands on the Euclidean section is derived inline (lines 123-132). It is the only way to discharge the `hne` hypothesis of `eqOn_of_eqOn_euclideanSection` from spacelike coverage, is independent of the analyticity argument, and Layer 0.3/0.4 (spacelike points vs. the Euclidean section) will need it; no consumer can get it from the public surface.

summary: The exposed surface is minimal and free of compatibility artifacts, and the general identity theorem is correctly public in the AnalyticOnNhd namespace. Two gaps: wickRotation's only structural property (that it matches the real points with the Euclidean section) exists in no lemma, and the reusable equal-time-projection fact is buried inside a proof body.
